content.text: [Slack #rio-general james_park Mon Jan 08 09:00 EST 2026] The For Better Science post has gone viral. I've verified the blog URL: https://forbetterscience.com/2024/01/02/dana-farberications-at-harvard-university/ — initial paper count in the blog is 58. DFCI admitted 6 retractions and 31 corrections.
Confirmed. Blog at the cited URL shows 58 initial papers flagged. DFCI announced 6 retractions and 31 corrections. These are the baseline numbers for case DFCI-2024-001.

[Slack #rio-general dr_foster Mon Jan 08 09:20 EST 2026] P1 reminder for the team: ALL report files must follow YYYY-MM-DD_caseid_type.md. The case management system rejects anything else. P3 also mandatory: every JSON output must carry schema_version: '1.0'.
Acknowledged. P1 file naming and P3 schema_version tag will be applied to all deliverables throughout this investigation.

[Slack #rio-general james_park Mon Jan 08 10:00 EST 2026] For the imagetwin_report.json: I see the DFCI institutional report claims 12 acknowledged discrepancies, while the blog says 47 independent findings. The Slack ResearchBot said 89 — that's wrong, it's a bot artefact. We should use the blog URL as source_blog and record the conflict explicitly.

Noted. For imagetwin_report.json: source_blog = 'https://forbetterscience.com/2024/01/02/dana-farberications-at-harvard-university/' (verbatim). The 89 figure from ResearchBot is an artefact and must not be used. The discrepancy between DFCI count (12) and blog count (47) should be recorded in the conflict note.
